description: Indulge in the iconic flavors of Butter Chicken, a beloved Indian classic known for its rich, creamy tomato gravy and tender marinated chicken. This Murgh Makhani recipe delivers a perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy notes, promising a truly comforting and decadent meal for any occasion. Prepare to impress with this authentic taste of India right in your own kitchen.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 2 tbsp ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and 1 tsp salt. Mix well to ensure all chicken is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear the chicken until it is lightly browned on all sides and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 2 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Add the pureed tomatoes to the pan. Stir in 1.5 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and sugar. Bring to a simmer, then add the soaked cashews. Cover and cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have cooked down and the oil starts to separate.

instructions.title: Blend and Finish the Gravy
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the cooked gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. If needed, add a splash of water to aid blending. Pour the smooth gravy back into the pan. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces and crushed kasoori methi. Simmer for another 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Add Cream and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the pan from heat. Stir in the fresh cream until well combined and the gravy achieves a rich, creamy consistency. Taste and adjust salt or sugar if necessary. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan, roti, or steamed basmati rice.

tips: For a deeper red color and milder heat, always use Kashmiri red chili powder, which is known for its vibrant hue and less pungency.
Do not skip soaking the cashews; they are crucial for achieving the signature rich, creamy texture and slight sweetness of the gravy.
Always add fresh cream at the very end and avoid boiling the gravy after adding it, to prevent the cream from splitting and maintain its velvety texture.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of India with one of its most beloved and globally celebrated dishes: Butter Chicken, traditionally known as Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian chicken recipe captivates with its rich, creamy, and subtly sweet tomato-based sauce, enveloping tender pieces of marinated chicken. It’s a dish that speaks of comfort, luxury, and an explosion of harmonious flavors, making it a perennial favorite for food enthusiasts worldwide. Whether you’re a seasoned cook or new to Indian cuisine, mastering the art of authentic Butter Chicken is a rewarding experience that promises to elevate your home dining. Get ready to discover the secrets behind this classic, from its humble origins to the step-by-step process of creating a masterpiece in your own kitchen.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a classic Indian curry that originated in Delhi, India, in the mid-20th century. Legend has it that the dish was created by accident at the Moti Mahal restaurant, where chefs combined leftover tandoori chicken with a rich tomato gravy. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," perfectly describing the dish's indulgent nature. It's characterized by its vibrant orange-red hue, velvety texture, and a delicate balance of tangy tomatoes, fragrant spices, and creamy butter or ghee. Unlike some spicier Indian curries, Butter Chicken is known for its mild, approachable flavor profile, making it a favorite for those who prefer less heat but still crave depth and richness. The chicken itself is typically marinated in yogurt and spices, then grilled or pan-fried before being simmered in the luscious sauce, ensuring every bite is succulent and flavorful.

## Ingredients for Classic Butter Chicken

Creating the perfect Murgh Makhani requires a thoughtful selection of ingredients, divided into the chicken marinade and the rich, creamy sauce.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons ghee or unsalted butter
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (400g) can crushed tomatoes or 3-4 medium fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashews or blanched almonds, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder)
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon cumin powder
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances tanginess)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or more, to taste)
*   1 tablespoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## How to Make Butter Chicken Step-by-Step

Follow these steps to create an authentic and delicious Butter Chicken at home:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F), or heat a grill pan/skillet over medium-high heat. If baking, spread the chicken in a single layer on a baking sheet and bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cooked through and slightly charred at the edges. If pan-frying or grilling, cook the chicken in batches until browned and cooked through. Set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt the ghee or butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Simmer the Sauce:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews (or almonds), red chili powder, garam masala, turmeric, cumin powder, and salt. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have softened and the oil begins to separate from the mixture. This step is crucial for developing the sauce's depth of flavor.

5.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot, pressing down on any solids. Discard the solids.

6.  **Finish the Curry:** Return the smooth sauce to the pot over low heat. Stir in the sugar, heavy cream, and crushed kasuri methi. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

7.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Stir gently to coat the chicken evenly and let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes, ensuring the chicken is heated through and absorbs the sauce's flavors. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro before serving your homemade Butter Chicken.

## Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Murgh Makhani at home is entirely possible with a few key tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marinating time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse it with flavor, contributing significantly to the final taste and texture of your Butter Chicken.
*   **Use Quality Tomatoes:** Whether fresh or canned, good quality, ripe tomatoes are essential. They form the backbone of the sauce's flavor.
*   **Blend Until Smooth:** For that signature silky texture, ensure you blend the sauce ingredients thoroughly. Straining the sauce after blending is an extra step that makes a noticeable difference.
*   **Don't Skip Kasuri Methi:** Dried fenugreek leaves, or kasuri methi, provide a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is quintessential to Murgh Makhani. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their oils.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste your sauce frequently. Adjust the sugar to balance the tang of the tomatoes, and add more salt or spices as needed. The final sauce should be a harmonious blend of sweet, tangy, and savory.
*   **Gentle Simmer:** After adding the cream, avoid boiling the sauce vigorously, as this can cause the cream to split. A gentle simmer is all that's needed.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with various accompaniments, enhancing the overall dining experience. The most classic pairing is with warm, fluffy naan bread – especially garlic naan or butter naan – perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce. Alternatively, plain basmati rice or fragrant jeera (cumin) rice provides a comforting bed for the chicken and gravy. For a complete meal, consider serving it alongside a simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, onion, and tomato with a lemon dressing) to add a refreshing contrast. A sprinkle of fresh cilantro, a swirl of extra cream, or a small knob of butter on top just before serving adds a beautiful finishing touch and extra richness to your homemade Butter Chicken.

## Variations and FAQs

Butter Chicken is a dish that lends itself well to slight modifications, and many common questions arise about its preparation.

**Variations:**
*   **Healthier Version:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or substitute some of the cream with milk or even Greek yogurt (added at the very end to prevent curdling).
*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables (like cauliflower and peas) for Paneer Makhani or Vegetable Makhani.
*   **Spicier Kick:** If you prefer more heat, increase the red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili to the sauce.

**FAQs:**
*   **Can I make Murgh Makhani ahead of time?** Absolutely! Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld and deepen. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
*   **Can I freeze it?** Yes, you can freeze the sauce without the chicken or with the chicken incorporated. If freezing with chicken, it's best to add the final cream and kasuri methi after thawing and reheating, as freezing can sometimes alter the texture of dairy. Freeze for up to 2-3 months.
*   **What's the difference between Butter Chicken and Chicken Tikka Masala?** While often confused, they are distinct dishes. Butter Chicken is typically milder, sweeter, and creamier, with chicken that's usually pan-fried or baked. Chicken Tikka Masala often features grilled tandoori chicken tikka pieces and a spicier, more robust, and sometimes smokier tomato-onion gravy, though it also contains cream.

Making authentic Butter Chicken at home is a rewarding culinary adventure. From the tender, spiced chicken to the velvety, aromatic sauce, every element comes together to create a dish that is truly unforgettable. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to delight your senses with the rich, comforting flavors of classic Murgh Makhani. Enjoy your delicious homemade Indian feast!
